title: Leibniz's Binary Arithmetic, Two Centuries Before Computers (1703)
explainer: Gottfried Leibniz worked out binary arithmetic in the late 1670s and published it formally in 1703 - more than two hundred years before any electronic computer existed - because he found the pattern of 0s and 1s mathematically and philosophically elegant, not because he needed it for engineering. Binary only became the representation real hardware uses much later, for a separate reason: a two-symbol system maps perfectly onto a two-state physical switch (on/off), which is exactly the physical constraint behind the encodings covered in this lesson.
